newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes firmer at 640-645 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes firmer at 640-645 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 640-645 per dollar, up from 665-675 in the morning, as foreign currency supply increased amid low lev liquidity following a rise of central bank minimum reserve requirements, dealers said.
"A lev shortage made banks and final clients sell dollars while demand was relatively low, which helped the lev rebound by some 30 from the opening," a commercial bank dealer said.
"Higher minimum reserve requirements will probably make banks continue paring foreign currency positions, but I do not expect any sharp lev appreciation," another dealer said. @

The BNB on Monday increased the volume of minimum required reserves for local commercial banks due this month to 11 percent of deposits banks have attracted in December from 10 percent in a bid to drain free lev liquidity and relieve pressure on the weakening lev.

Banks would have to place some 20 billion levs more with the central bank to meet the higher requirements this month, bringing the total to some 105 billion levs according to preliminary estimates, a BNB official told Reuters. @
The central bank was not seen buying dollars amid the increased dollar supply today, traders said. BNB officials were not available for comment.
